_about: Screening dictionary for model input features in Indian hiring. Rules are checked in priority order (PROTECTED, STRONG_PROXY, MODERATE_PROXY, JOB_RELATED); the highest-priority match sets the category. Any feature that matches nothing is UNCLASSIFIED and needs a written job-relatedness justification: the default is to justify, not to assume neutrality.

actions.PROTECTED: Remove from model inputs. May be collected only voluntarily, separately from the model, for fairness auditing.
actions.STRONG_PROXY: Remove unless a documented job analysis shows it is necessary for the role and an audit shows no adverse impact; if kept, test it explicitly.
actions.MODERATE_PROXY: Keep only with a written job-relatedness justification and a bias test of this feature.
actions.JOB_RELATED: Acceptable in principle; confirm it is measured the same way for every candidate and is validated for this role.
actions.UNCLASSIFIED: Proposer must justify its relevance to the job before it can be used.

rules.rationale: Gender, including transgender identity, is a prohibited ground in recruitment (Code on Wages, 2019 s. 3; Transgender Persons Act, 2019 ss. 3 and 9).
Age is not a valid predictor of ability; policy POL-AI-04 treats it as protected.
Caste discrimination is constitutionally condemned (Arts. 15, 17) and a recurrent pattern in Indian hiring research.
Religion is a protected characteristic (Art. 15; policy POL-AI-04).
Marital status is used against women in hiring; it has no bearing on job ability.
RPwD Act, 2016 requires equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation.
Pregnancy and family status are direct routes to gender discrimination.
A photograph reveals several protected characteristics at once.
Irrelevant to the job; protected under policy POL-AI-04.
In India a name often signals caste, religion, region and gender together. Audit studies have repeatedly found callback gaps by name.
Residential segregation makes locality a proxy for community and income.
Region of origin is a proxy for language, community and migrant status.
Mother tongue maps closely to region and community.
Parental occupation and background encode caste and class.

rules.pattern: \b(graduation year|year of graduation|passing year|year of passing|batch year)\b
rules.rationale: Graduation year lets a model recover age almost exactly.
Career gaps are common after marriage, maternity, caregiving and illness; penalising them penalises women and people with disabilities.
Access to elite institutions is unequal by class, caste and region; 'tier' rankings carry that inequality into scores.
Accent reflects region and schooling, not ability, and disadvantages speech-related disabilities.
Scores inferred from faces or behaviour are affect inference (red line RL-01) and penalise cultural, neurodivergent and disabled candidates.
Physical appearance is rarely job-related and carries colourism and gender bias.
Acceptable as a minimum; as an upper bound or a continuous score it becomes an age proxy.
Legitimate only where the role needs the language; then test it directly rather than infer it.
Schooling medium reflects family resources, not ability.
Prestige of past employers compounds earlier inequalities of access.
Salary history imports the gender pay gap into new decisions.
Proxy for neighbourhood; ask instead whether the candidate can meet working hours.
Leisure activities reflect money and gender norms more than ability.
Online activity is unequally distributed and raises consent and purpose questions.
Marks vary by board and region; use only with role-specific justification and normalisation.
Short tenures can reflect caregiving, relocation after marriage or contract work.

rules.pattern: \b(skills? test|skill assessment|aptitude|work sample|job simulation|assessment score|case exercise|situational judg\w*)\b
rules.rationale: Direct measures of job-relevant ability, given to every candidate the same way.
Structured interviews with fixed questions and rubrics are among the most valid and fair selection methods.
Legally or technically required credentials for the role.
Job-relevant if defined from a job analysis and extracted accurately.
